Instead of trying to attack the Jade Palace, they slowly spread along the edges of the great bridge, forming two columns that stretched from one of its ends to the other.

And then, silently, they climbed to stand on the parapets.

Kai paled.

"What about now, Kai? Do you feel like surrendering yet?"

Seishans pleasant, raspy voice made him shiver.

Not receiving an answer, she sighed.

"Be it your way."

Kai flinched.

Summer Knight could not see, but he witnessed it in flawless detail. Far in the distance, the two people closest to the opposite end of the bridge silently took a step forward and plummeted into the bottomless chasm below.

Their silhouettes disappeared into the ash blizzard a few moments later, as if erased from existence.

That was what it looked like to everyone but Kai, who could easily see through the ash.

Seishan looked at him with a smile.

"How about now?"

The next pair fell down.

"Not yet?"

Kai simply stood there, frozen.

"Stop."

Seishan sighed.

"Im afraid I cannot stop."

Two more people plummeted to their deaths.

"Stop."

She looked at him with pity.

"Only you can stop this, Kai."

Two more.

And then, another two.

And then...

"Stop. Stop!"

Seishan laughed.

"They will only stop when you surrender. Are you still hesitating?"

Kai shuddered.

She let out a quiet sigh.

"Look. Your hesitation has already cost dozens of lives."

Seishan looked at him, the smile leaving her scarlet lips.

"How many more people must die because of your inaction?"

Kai simply stood there, frozen... just like the people whom he had commanded to halt were frozen in front of him, unable to move.

The steel colossus of the Lord of Shadows remained motionless, as well, awaiting Kais command.

By his side, Summer Knight spared the Steward of the West a grim look, then gritted his teeth and lunged forward.

His sword was aimed at Seishan, but it never reached her.

Her sisters moved to intercept him, batting the sword away and raining blows on his armor.

"You... wretched..."

Gilead would not be swayed by the plague... which made him incapable of becoming a subject for the Hunger Domain, and therefore useless to Asterion. So, the Song sisters did not hold back their killing intent.

At the same time, he was not a part of the Longing Domain. So, Changing Star could not heal his wounds.

He should have been crushed under an avalanche of their attacks... but, somehow, Gilead broke through the barrier of steel created by the Song sisters and rushed toward Seishan.

His armor was broken and torn, but his body was only covered by minor lacerations. His sword was still sharp and steady.

Seishan tilted her head, looking at him.

As Summer Knight took the next step, the minor wounds on his body began to bleed.

A step more, and the trickles of blood that flowed from his wounds turned into streams.

Another step, and his bleeding turned gruesomely dire.

Summer Knight slowed down, swaying, then gritted his teeth and took the next step.

By the time he reached Seishan, he resembled a ghastly red statue. The remains of his polished armor were painted entirely red, and his face was like a glistening crimson mask.

"He said... stop..."

Despite Summer Knights horrid state, his low voice remained clear.

His sword trembled as it rose arduously, straining to reach Seishans neck.

But in the end, it clattered to the ground.

Seishan did not move, but Summer Knight swayed, then fell down and grew still, the crown of his head resting near her feet.

A puddle of blood spread around his body, soaking the hem of her dress.

And behind her, two more people stopped off the bridge into the ashen abyss.

Kai looked down, dazed.

"Gilead..."

There was...

There was so much blood.

...That day, Seishan of Clan Song became the master of the Jade Palace.

Chapter 2821: Above Deck

Chapter 2821: Above Deck

In another memory, Soul Reaper Jet was looking down at the vast expanse of the Night Garden as life slowly flowed out of her broken soul, drop by drop like it always did.

Bringing a golden fruit to her mouth, she took a bite and chewed its flesh slowly, a thoughtful expression on her face.

She spared the fruit a long look.

"Eating fruits every day..."

She had never even seen a fruit during her time in the outskirts, let alone tasted one.

Life was sure full of surprises. It was full of unexpected outcomes, as well.

Taking another bite, she continued to study the lively expanse of the layered decks far below.

Things were turning strange on the Night Garden.

The ship was currently gliding through the boundless abyss of the dark sky below the Chained Isles. There was nothing but an endless emptiness above it. Beneath it, meanwhile, was a furious sea of fire it was as if the Night Garden was sailing above the surface of a star.

The heat rising from the ocean of divine flame was keeping the titanic ship afloat in the empty abyss. Not in the sense that it was gliding on the rising currents of warm air, though rather, the hull of the Night Garden was soaking in the heat and turning it into torrents of essence to sustain its innate sorcery.

Which was good news, since the ship was consuming a great amount of essence now that it was sailing on air instead of water. That was something it had become capable of after being mended and restored at the wharf of the Eternal City, among other things.

Making the Night Garden fly had actually turned out to be quite simple. It had never relied on the winds or propulsion engines to sail, after all instead, it moved due to the divine sorcery left behind by the Demon of Repose. So, if its helmsman was skilled and powerful enough, the living ship could easily sail on air instead of water... or even on nothing at all, if need be.

It was just that the amount of essence required to lift it into the air was too taxing for a Transcendent captain. Beings of such a measly Rank were quite obviously not meant to control the living vessel, and since they could not substitute the essence the Night Garden consumed with their own, an external source was needed to keep it in the air for prolonged periods of time.

Something like a raging storm... or a sea of divine flames burning in a vast abyss.

The mission to evacuate the citizens of the Sanctuary of Noctis had been both sudden and ambitious. The Night Garden traveled to the Chained Isles through the Dream Gate, steered by the Saints of Night Naeve, Aether, Bloodwave, and Nightwalker himself. With the four of them rotating at the helm, the living ship could barely be kept afloat.

The Night Garden arrived at the Sanctuary the city that now sprawled across half a dozen islands around the Sanctuary of Noctis where the entire local population hastily boarded it. Saint Tyris and Saint Roan, as well as the Awakened warriors of the White Feather clan, joined them as well.

Then, the living ship dove into the Sky Below just before the King of Nothing descended upon the Chained Isles from the Hollow Mountains.

And here they were, drifting above the sea of flames. Nephis had departed to wherever it was she had gone, and the Human Domain was slowly collapsing somewhere far above them.

The Night Garden was severely overpopulated at the moment, and although everyone lived in cramped conditions, there was enough food for everyone. There were also seven Saints aboard: Jet, Nightwalker, Bloodwave, Aether, Naeve, Tyris, and Roan. So even if they ran out of some supplies, they could bring more from the waking world.

The problem lay somewhere else.

Taking another bite of the fruit, Jet narrowed her eyes as she scrutinized the movement of people on the main decks of the Night Garden.

Everything seemed in order. However, something felt off to her eyes. There were invisible undercurrents and signs of internal strife that werent that difficult to notice, but there was something else, too.

She knew that most of the mundane population of her Citadel had already succumbed to the plague of Asterion. The loyalty of the Awakened warriors was questionable, as well. There were plenty of ways to confirm that someone still belonged to the Longing Domain, but Jet doubted that any of them were truly trustworthy.

In fact, she was willing to bet that even if there was no reasonable way to fool the tests, the Dreamspawn had long found a way to do just that.

Everyone acted like they used to, but at the same time, many people raised her suspicion. So, Jet and the other Saints, as well as the Ascended officers under their command, had been carefully positioning the troops they deemed trustworthy or at least hoped that they were near the vital elements of the living ships ecosystem.

The loyalists and the turncoats... the believers and the apostates... aboard the Night Garden were constantly getting into small conflicts, and the soldiers under Jets command were busy making sure that things did not get out of hand.

The living ship was like a powder keg, and days passed in the atmosphere of distrust and tension.

It felt like a mutiny was brewing.

Jet chewed on the golden fruit calmly.

If the mundane population of the Night Garden rebelled... even if the Awakened soldiers joined them, they would not be able to gain control of the living ship. That was simply because they would not be able to defeat the seven Saints who guarded it.

However, Jet did not suspect only the mundane people and the Awakened. She was an equal opportunity offender, so she did not fully trust her Ascended officers, either, and was watching the other six Saints even Nightwalker with a wary eye, too.

There were definitely questionable things about them. There were more and more strange discrepancies Jet noticed every day... if it wasnt all in her head.

They were probably having the same thoughts about her.

Chapter 2822: Something to Lose

Chapter 2822: Something to Lose

Yesterday, Jet had shared a bottle of strong spirits with Nightwalker. The conversation was relaxed, but inevitably turned to their current predicament.

"The ship absorbs an ocean of essence from the divine flame, but climbing up to the surface will be difficult. We can train young Tyris and her husband to steer the ship, but even with six Saints working in shifts, well run ourselves ragged."

She gave him a curious glance.

"What are you getting at?"

Nightwalker looked her up and down, then grinned.

"Well, your pool of essence is several times deeper than that of any of us. Plus, youre the captain. It seems strange that you are not standing at the helm, no? Wont you take at least a shift or two?"

Jet studied him with a relaxed smile.

Nothing of what he said was wrong, but she had removed herself from the rotation for a reason. When the Saints of Night steered the Night Garden through the air, all they had to do after a shift was spend a few days replenishing their essence. Jet could not do the same, though instead, she would have to hunt a significant number of Nightmare Creatures to refill her shattered core.

Which was not a problem, usually... however, she would be vulnerable until she did. If someone wanted to eliminate her, that would be the perfect moment to attack.

Was Nightwalker really asking her to take the helm because he wanted to spare the rest of the Saints some exhaustion, or was there a more sinister intent behind his request?

She took a sip of alcohol and shrugged, her smile remaining the same.

"Ill think about it."

A day before that, Naeve had been making a routine report to her.

"There were a total of twenty-four violent altercations between the civilians yesterday. Fifteen connected to the strife between the Domains, the rest due to mundane reasons. Bruises and lacerations, nothing serious. The troublemakers were detained to let them cool down."

He checked his notes.

"The food stores are holding up well. A few are depleted, but we are almost ready to harvest the innermost fields. That should cover the difference. All in all, our surplus seems sufficient to feed the additional population. Theres nothing else to report, really."

Jet nodded.

"Good."

She glanced at him briefly, then asked in a neutral tone.

"Oh, by the way. Did you change the guard shifts in the Mainmast Pagoda a few days back?"

Naeve remained silent for a moment, checking his notes again. After shuffling through several pages, he nodded.

"Yes, there was a minor change."

Jet raised an eyebrow.

"Why?"

He shrugged.

"A few soldiers were seen fraternizing with the turncoats, so I had to replace them. That, in turn, required pushing the shift change timing a bit."

Jet remained silent.

She wouldnt call changing security personnel a minor issue. Even if it was, why hadnt Naeve informed her?

Was it strange, or was she just being paranoid?

She smiled, then looked away and nodded.

"Okay."

At some point between these two conversations, Jet was showing Sky Tide around the ship. They talked as they moved between the decks.

"Anyway. I hear that your daughter has run off to challenge a Nightmare?"

Tyris pursed her lips.

"She did."

Jet studied her briefly, then chuckled quietly.

"Like father, like daughter. The apple does not fall far from the tree, huh?"

Tyris sighed and fell silent. Eventually, though, she asked:

"Is that where our Sovereign is? Has she run off to challenge the Fifth Nightmare?"

Jet spared her another look. The champions of the Human Domain were naturally curious about where Changing Star was, considering that the world seemed to be falling apart at an appalling speed.

"As I said before, I do not know."

She wasnt lying. Jet herself did not know where Nephis and Sunny had disappeared to, only that they had gone to complete a vital mission. Even Cassie did not seem to know, despite the fact that she had been the one to inform them about that development.

Tyris frowned.

"Do you really not know, or are you only saying that you dont know?"

Jet turned to look at her.

It was natural for Sky Tide to want to know where the Supreme she had sworn to serve was. However... that was the third time she had asked Jet, despite receiving the same answer the first two times.

Was she really asking out of concern... or was she asking because someone else really, really wanted to know where his opponents were?

"I really dont know."

Tyris did not ask her the same question again, but woould stare at her strangely from time to time after that.

All of it was quite distressing. The suspicion, the ambiguity, the waiting... it was honestly a bit tiring.

Jet almost wished that, if something were to happen, it would happen already.

I wonder... can I defeat all six, if things devolve into bloodshed?

She exhaled slowly.

Tyris and Roan had the terrain advantage here, in the Sky Below. Naeve and Bloodwave were at a disadvantage instead. Aether... she wasnt sure how his Aspect and the divine flames influenced each other, so it was hard to tell.

Nightwalker was an old monster who was utterly lethal in any environment, as well as the one she was most wary of.

Still...

If Jet had to bet, she would bet on herself.

If they were to attack her, shed probably kill at least most of them.

Maybe even all of them.

She really wished they wouldnt, though. Chances were, they were not going to.

There were easier ways to defeat her than a battle, after all.

There was an entire ship of people under her command, and each of those people could become a hostage. What was she going to do if the Saint at the helm of the Night Garden threatened to drop it into the ocean of divine flames unless she surrendered?

What would she do if they forced her to calculate the value of her own life against the unknown number of lives she was meant to protect?

The golden fruit were usually sweet, but today, the one she had plucked tasted bitter.

Jet sighed.

"Life is indeed full of surprises. But, strangely... I miss the days when I had nothing to lose..."

Chapter 2823: Excess Heat

Chapter 2823: Excess Heat

Days passed while the Night Garden drifted through the vast emptiness of the Sky Below.

Far above, the King of Nothing had already conquered the Glass Hell and the Chained Isles. Now, his forces were invading Godgrave and the Moonriver Plains, as well as moving south, toward the distant Black Mountains.

The Black Mountains had served as the boundary of the lands tamed by humanity once, decades ago. Then, Anvil and Madoc of Valor led their Knights on a conquest crusade to subjugate the regions of the Dream Realm laying further north, eventually reaching all the way to the Hollow Mountains.

Now, Mordret was taking the lands they had conquered back from humanity. It was as if he were erasing everything his father had achieved, one feat at a time.

I guess its a little poetic... in a morbidly sinister kind of way.

Jet was descending toward the runic hall of the Mainmast Pagoda.

There, Nightwalker was currently at the helm of the living ship. The two of them had been busy for the last few days, working closely together to develop an alternative way of escaping the Sky Below.

The simplest way was to ascend the same way they had descended slowly and arduously, pouring oceans of essence into the Night Garden. The obvious drawbacks of this method were that it would exhaust the Saints, as well as that they would escape the abyss in the middle of the Chained Isles, which currently belonged to Mordret.

The more difficult way was to use one of the living ships Components to open a portal to somewhere else.

Opening spatial rifts and moving through them was one of the abilities Night Garden had gained after visiting the Eternal City. The problem was that, like many of its other Continents, it was not really meant to be used by a Saint. Jet could open a portal, but only as far as her eyes could see which was largely meaningless, since the living ship could breach that gap in no time all by itself.

To truly make use of that function of the living ship, they had to master a different one first a function that had to do with navigation. However, no matter how much time they spent on studying it, the puzzle still remained unsolved.

In the end, Jet could not open a portal to guide the Night Garden away from the Sky Below and the Chained Isles she wasnt a good enough navigator for that.

However... there was Nightwalker.

He not only possessed the lineage of Storm God, the god of travel and guidance, but also had an Aspect Ability that allowed him to always know where to go in order to get to where he wanted to arrive.

So, in theory, Nightwalker did not even need to master the navigation tools of the Night Garden. As long as they could properly integrate his Aspect into the sorcery of the living ship, he would probably be able to open a portal to almost anywhere without having to master a different function of the ship.

That was what Jet and Nightwalker had been working on ever since the Night Garden plunged into the Sky Below, and by now, it felt like they were nearing a turning point.

All the while, the plague of Asterion was ravaging the population of the living ship, and paranoia was slowly taking over the Saints who were meant to protect it.

Jet entered the runic hall and nodded at Nightwalker, who was standing in the circle.

"How is it?"

He gave her an apologetic smile.

"Sorry. I havent been able to make any progress since yesterday."

Jet remained silent for a few moments, looking at him.

Then, she smiled as well.

"Okay."

Wasnt he saying that he could almost feel the connection yesterday?

She chose not to comment.

Instead, she turned to the other two people present in the runic hall. They were Naeve and Aether, discussing something quietly among themselves.

"And what are you two doing here?"

Distracted from their conversation, they greeted her warmly.

"Oh, we are just waiting for my uncle."

Naeve seemed inpatient.

In recent days, the Saints under her command had taken it upon themselves to take turns traveling to the waking world. There, they gathered information about the current situation, as well as procured various supplies that the ship needed.

Aether glanced at Naeve, then politely offered a more detailed explanation:

"He is supposed to bring a civil engineer who can help us deal with the excess heat. The ship is overcrowded, and with all those flames below us, people are quite uncomfortable. So, we hope to quite literally cool them off. If we do, maybe the amount of problems they create will lessen."

Heat waves had always been known to increase the crime rate. The living ship was already like a powder keg, so their motive seemed reasonable.

At least at first glance... as long as one did not think too hard about it.

Jet studied them quietly.

"Good thinking."

The compliment was hollow.

At that moment, there was the sound of steps, and two more Saints suddenly appeared in the runic hall. They were Tyris and Roan, looking around with reserved curiosity.

Jet spared them a confused look.

"And why are you here?"

Roan flashed her a charismatic smile.

"Nightwalker insisted that we learn how to steer this ship, in case we need to help out with supplying it with essence. So, we are here for a lesson."

Nightwalker waved from the runic circle.

"Right, right! Just wait for me quietly. You can observe what I do in the meantime."

Jet remained silent.

It made sense that Nightwalker would want to teach Tyrs and Roan how to control the ship. They indeed needed more hands, considering how much essence the Night Garden would consume as it left the sea of flames behind.

However...

Jet looked around carefully.

Nightwalker was in front of her. Naeve and Aether were flanking her. Tyris and Roa, meanwhile, were still standing at the entrance.

Cutting off her path of escape.

Was it a coincidence, or a trap?

Jet suddenly felt a cold shiver run down his spine.

And was Bloodwave really bridging in a civil engineer?

Just as she thought that, two figures appeared in the grand emptiness of the runic hall.

One of them was the familiar tall Saint of the House of Night.

The other...

Had golden eyes.

Chapter 2824: Civil Engineering

Chapter 2824: Civil Engineering

Just a few moments before Bloodwave and the uninvited guest appeared in the runic hall of the Night Garden, Jet, who had been looking at her fellow Saints with a wary expression, smiled suddenly.

She turned to Nightwalker.

"You know what? I think Ill take that shift, after all. You look exhausted."

He raised an eyebrow.

"Oh, really?"

Jet was already stepping into the runic circle.

She maintained an easy smile as a cold shiver ran down her spine.

"Whats this? You dont seem happy at all. After complaining so much..."

She patted him on the shoulder and gently pushed him out of the circle. Nightwalker seemed a little reluctant, but he did not have a reason to refuse, so he left without saying anything.

By then, the silhouettes of two people were already forming in the air.

As the captain of the Night Garden, Jet was always connected to it. However, that connection was usually subtle and vague, existing in the deep periphery of her subconscious mind. It was only when she stepped into the runic circle that the connection opened fully, allowing her to share the feelings of the living ship and exert precise control over it.

Now, too, she suddenly both remained herself and became a vast presence that bathed in the nurturing heat of divine flames as her body sheltered and nurtured millions of living beings in turn.

Time seemed to slow down for a moment.

Jet could only see the vague silhouettes of Bloodwave as the civil engineer he was supposed to bring as they were manifested in the Dream Realm.

However, the Night Garden felt their arrival far more deeply. One was familiar and caring. The other was a stranger, his presence as vast as an ocean and full of endless, insatiable hunger... and kinship, as well.

The stranger bore the scent of Heart God and its sacred forest.

Jets smile faltered.

A civil engineer, my foot.

Before she could react, Bloodwave and the man he carried across the realm boundary fully materialized on the floor of the runic hall. The supposed engineer was tall and imposing, looking at her with two beautiful golden eyes.

He was none other than Supreme Asterion, the Dreamspawn, in the flesh.

Jet felt her blood running cold.

She had expected an ambush... but she had not expected that.

As Asterion looked around the bridge of the Night Garden with curiosity, the other Saints Naeve, Aether, Bloodwave, Tyris, Roan, and even Nightwalker bowed.

"Welcome, my lord."

The corner of Jets mouth twitched as she spared Nightwalker a dark look.

Him too? After all the torment and horror he had endured because of the Dreamspawn?

...Or had he been a thrall of the Dreamspawn this whole time?

No, it couldnt be.

Jets mood soured.

Still, she mentally patted herself on the back. Her distrust of the other Saints had turned out to be justified if there was one thing that had never failed her in this life, it was paranoia.

Finally, Asterions gaze settled on Jet. She met it steadily, trying her best not to appear rattled.

He smiled.

"Ah, Soul Reaper Jet. What a charming nickname. It is a pleasure to meet you... oh, but you dont seem to be surprised to see me at all?"

Jet remained silent for a few moments, then forced on a faint smile of her own.

"On the contrary. I am quite shocked."

She glanced at the Saints that were scattered around the runic hall, surrounding her, and shrugged.

"I was expecting that the six of them would try to subdue me with an unexpected attack. Never in my wildest dreams did I imagine that Lord Asterion himself would come to deal with this humble Transcendent."

He chuckled.

"A humble Transcendent? Please, dont sell yourself short."

Asterion studied Jet with a hint of amusement in his golden eyes.

"Ive met all kinds of people, you know? Powerful people, cunning people, great masters of warfare and the like... even people whose main virtue was that they were inexplicably lucky, which made them more dangerous than all the rest. And among all those people, youd still rank as one of the most impressive, Miss Jet."

Jet scoffed.

"What is this, flattery?"

He shrugged.

"No, no... Im simply stating the facts. Everyone has a weakness, you see. But not all weaknesses can be easily exploited. Powerful people, cunning people, lucky people, and great masters of all kinds dealing with them poses no problem at all. To tell you the truth, I wasnt planning to act personally at this stage, since delegating tasks to my subordinates was more than sufficient."

Asterion sighed.

"But no matter how much I tried, I couldnt see a way for them to deal with Soul Reaper Jet. Not without sacrificing more talents than I am willing to sacrifice, at least, or without destroying you instead of making you mine. It is quite an accomplishment, really... I cant believe that we all overlooked such a gem, all those years ago."

He looked at Jet and smiled brightly.

"So, I had to come and deal with you myself. There are only two Transcendents who managed to make me act personally, by the way. Well done."

Jet studied him with a grim expression.

"...What an honor."

Asterion laughed.

"I feel a note of sarcasm in your voice, but actually, it is indeed an honor. You should feel proud."

Jet studied him for a few moments, then sighed.

"You know, people like me those who grew up in the outskirts dont like the word honor that much. In fact, one might say that we cant stand it."

He raised an eyebrow, looking at her with curiosity.

"The outskirts? I am sorry, but I am not familiar with the term. Is that something from your world?"

A grin slowly bloomed on Jets lips.

"Right. Youre not from Earth, so you might not know. Yes, its a term from the waking world. The outskirts are where the non-citizens lived, and they had a peculiar culture. People from the outskirts those who live long enough to escape them, at least are known to be distrustful, vicious, cynical, and tenacious. They often share common traits, as well."

She took a deep breath and looked around the runic hall, coldly evaluating the Sovereign and the six Saints that surrounded her.

"Like, for example..."

The runes of the circle shimmered slightly, and a subtle change spread across the hall.

Jet smiled darkly.

"They tend to never enter a room without an exit strategy..."

Chapter 2825: Exit Strategy

Chapter 2825: Exit Strategy

A while back, Jet had asked herself if she would be able to kill the six Saints aboard the Night Garden if they were to conspire against her.

She had also asked herself what she would do if the entire population of the living ship was taken hostage or turned on her.

The answer to the first question was... yes, probably. She could not be sure, but deep down, she knew that they would not survive a battle against her. Her Aspect was simply too deadly, and the gap in physical prowess between her and the rest of the Saints was simply too vast in that regard, she was closer to a Supreme than to a Transcendent.

Besides all that... she was simply a killer. That innate quality was hard to define or measure, but those who knew its lethal scent could easily distinguish between those who possessed it and those who did not. Needless to say, the former was many times more dangerous.

It was just that slaying six powerful Saints would not help anyone. Whether she managed to kill them or not, humanity would suffer a grievous loss so, what was the point in trying?

As for the second question, Jet was honestly not sure. She did, however, know that if things ever came to that, the battle would have already been lost.

And while she would have fought for the cause of her people to the last drop of blood if there was a smallest possibility of victory, only a fool would continue to bleed themselves dry in a battle that had already ended in defeat.

Saving herself to fight another day was an option, too, even if it meant surrendering the Night Garden and millions of souls to the enemy. After all, she would not be able to snatch them from Asterions grasp even if she stayed.

So, Jet had been hoping for the best while preparing for the worst possible outcome in secret.

She was ready to escape instead of fighting the six Saints.

Sadly... she had really not expected that Asterion would come for her personally.

His presence here complicated things. A lot.

Looking at Jet, Asterion chuckled.

"It does complicate things, doesnt it?"

Jets expression darkened.

She remained silent for a few moments, then said in a disgruntled tone:

"Its impolite to read a ladys private thoughts."

Asterion simply shrugged.

"Its also impolite to cast all your thoughts and emotions outward as if you were screaming at the top of your lungs constantly, incessantly, for everyone to hear. Noise, noise, noise... you people are noisy enough to drive a person mad. Its deafening. I spent a long time learning how to stay sane in the endless cacophony of your souls."

His lips twisted into a friendly smile.

"So, forgive me for taking a peek at your plans of escape. Granted, youve been cunning enough to hide the details of how exactly you were going to run away even from your own mind... but that shouldnt matter too much."

The friendly smile suddenly seemed menacing.

"Should it, Miss Jet?"

Jet blinked, having caught herself staring into his golden eyes.

Wait...

What... what had she been thinking about?

Jet knew that she had prepared an escape strategy. However, no matter how much she tried to remember what it was, she couldnt. It was as if there was an empty space in her mind where her plan had been... or maybe a tall wall that prevented her from accessing these thoughts.

She tried to hide her fear and looked at Asterion with the same somber expression.

"Thats a neat trick. However, do you really think that you can keep me here against my will? I am quite good at improvising as well, you know."

Asterion laughed.

"I know. But why would you want to leave?"

Jet blinked again, confused.

Indeed. Why would she want to leave?

She vaguely remembered wanting to escape, but could not comprehend why. This was her Citadel, after all. Her people were here; her home was here, too, as well as her beautiful garden.

There seemed to be no reason to leave the Night Garden, and every reason to stay.

Asterion sighed in satisfaction.

"There. Thats better."

Jet looked at him in a daze.

No, wait. Something is not right here.

It felt like she had forgotten something.

But what was it? She couldnt put her finger on it.

The other Saints moved, slowly getting closer to the runic circle. Asterion took a step forward, as well, his golden eyes holding her gaze.

"Now, let us..."

But before he could finish the sentence, something strange happened.

Instead of landing on the wooden floor, his foot seemed to sink into it, making Asterion stumble. An expression of surprise appeared on his face, replaced a moment later by a pained grimace.

"Miss Jet. Is your ship... trying to eat me, by any chance?"

Asterion, Nightwalker, and the rest of the Saints were slowly sinking into the floor, as if it were quicksand instead of solid wood. Watching that, Jet frowned thoughtfully.

Then, she smiled.

"Ah! I remember now. The plan I improvised."

Asterion stared at her for a moment, then snarled.

He moved, and the wooden floor around him exploded into splinters. At the same time, Nightwalker who had been standing closest to Jet flicked his wrist, sending an ominously gleaming throwing knife at her.

The enchanted knife hit Jet in the chest... and passed through her, as if flying through mist.

She gave him a bitter look.

"Bastard. Well talk about it later..."

In the next moment, Asterion was standing near her, his hand stretching forward to grab her neck.

But before he could...

Jet vanished without a trace, as if she had never been there.

At the same time, she appeared far below, on the main deck of the Night Garden. Jet lost her balance, fell into a roll, and slid a few meters before jumping to her feet.

All around her, hundreds of people thousands, maybe were all staring at her with ominous expressions. Some of them were mundane, some were Awakened, and more than a few were Masters.

All of them, however, seemed to have been enthralled by the Dreamspawn already.

Im surrounded by zombies...

No. Was she the zombie?

Now that Jet was far away from the Dreamspawn, her mind seemed to have been freed from the hex. So, she could remember what she had been planning to do, and why.

Escape, huh...

It was easier said than done when a demented Sovereign was hot on her heels.

Chapter 2826: Delegated Escape

Chapter 2826: Delegated Escape

Jet realized that all her plans had become meaningless the moment she felt Asterions presence through the Night Garden.

Dealing with six powerful Saints was already difficult enough. Dealing with six Saints and a damn Supreme on top of that was... well above her paygrade. Now that Asterion boarded the Night Garden, executing her escape would be all but impossible, and on top of that, his Aspect granted him frightening powers.

The moment he appeared in the runic hall, he would be able to read her mind and learn how exactly she was planning to get away. Even worse, he would be able to manipulate her very thoughts, twisting them and turning her own mind against her.

Jet prided herself on being paranoid, but now, she couldnt even trust herself.

She had to improvise an entirely new plan of escape in the brief moment between the vague silhouettes of Bloodwave and Asterion appearing in the runic hall and them fully crossing the realm boundary, manifesting in the Dream Realm not only that, but she had to make that plan impervious to the powers of the malevolent Sovereign, somehow.

So, she did just that.

By the time Asterion laid eyes on her, the new plan had already been put in place. Jet also made an effort to focus all her thoughts on the old one, forbidding herself from thinking about anything else.

It seemed to be working, for now.

She had not been certain that it would. Her new plan was quite simple, but also innately devious in its simplicity. It relied on a single proposition that while Asterion could manipulate and deceive her own mind, even he could not manipulate the vast, slumbering mind of the Night Garden.

The Night Garden was not just any ship, after all. It was a living ship, and while it did not quite possess a consciousness in the way people understood the concept, it was not truly mindless either.

So, in that brief moment before Asterion appeared in the runic hall, Jet gave the Night Garden a simple command.

Protect its captain.

That was why the Dreamspawn and the Saints he had subjugated suddenly started to sink into the floor. The Mainmast Pagoda and the floor of the runic hall were carved from the same wood as the hull of the living ship the Night Garden had never absorbed and digested its passengers, but not because it could not.

Rather, it was because it had been damaged in the past, and there was no reason to consume the beings it was meant to shelter and nurture anyway.

Jet doubted that Asterion and the Saints would be seriously harmed by that simple defensive measure, but they had at least been slowed down at a decisive moment.

Next, the Night Garden sent her away from the runic hall, where the danger was, to its main deck. Jet suspected that it had opened a miniature portal between the two just like it could open a vast rift in space to travel from one place to another.

So... something like that was possible, too.

The sudden break of the connection between Jet and the living ship was a bit jarring, but she swiftly regained her senses.

She was standing on one of the outer decks of the Night Garden now, surrounded from all sides by hostile thralls of the Dreamspawn. Asterion was already aware of her current location, no doubt. He would escape the runic hall in a matter of moments, so...

She needed to run.

There was nowhere to run in the Sky Below, really. The Night Garden was surrounded by a vast emptiness from all sides except for one, where a sea of divine flames burned in the darkness.

However, Jet was a Saint, and Saints could always escape across the realm boundary to a different world.

It was just that pulling on ones tether required time and concentration.

Jet had little time and could not afford to focus entirely on her tether. Still, she had to manage it, somehow.

Just when a small figure exploded from the arched portals of the runic hall far above, at the top of the Mainmast Pagoda, she lunged into a run. She had to buy herself more time, and there was only one way to do it.

From where she stood, only a few hundred meters separated her from the edge of the Night Garden, beyond which lay the empty dark void a distance that a Saint could breach in the blink of an eye. When people moved to bar her way, Jet simply turned into a mist and flowed past them, rushing toward the railing.

However, bizarrely, it took her several seconds just to move a few dozen steps.

Jet cursed.

Nightwalker, that old lecher!

The legendary Saint was twisting space to increase the distance between her and the dark void. He couldnt stop her entirely, but he could slow her down.

Somewhere above her, two flying figures dove out of the towering pagoda following the first they were Tyris and Roan, without a doubt.

Behind her, meanwhile, Asterion landed on the deck of the Night Garden like a meteor.

Damn it.

Jet poured a roaring torrent of essence into her muscles. Her dead body was special, as it could absorb far more essence than the flesh of the living could so, she could move faster than almost any Saint, streaking across the deck like lightning.

But not as fast as Asterion was moving as he lunged after her. The Dreamspawn did not even seem to run; he simply blinked out of existence at one spot and appeared in the next in the blink of an eye, he was already upon her.

It was then that the Night Garden suddenly tilted, throwing Asterion off balance while simultaneously pushing Jet toward her goal.

She leaped onto a massive cannon that stood in front of the railing, then jumped into the empty space below.

An arrow pierced her shoulder at the last moment, wounding her and making her bleed.

Jet was spun around as she fell, witnessing the beautiful sight of the countless lanterns that illuminated the Night Garden for the last time.

Goodbye, my wondreous ship. Thank you. I hope well meet again...

Then, she plummeted down, into the depths of the Sky Below and the furious radiance of the ocean of flame that burned beneath her.

This... is going to hurt.

Watching two enormous figures a magnificent bird of prey and a winged lion diving to catch her, Jet focused on her tether.

She fell, and fell, and fell... as she did, the blinding radiance of divine flames grew more intense around her.

The heat was suffocating at first.

Then, when Jet crossed the invisible barrier of the living ships aegis, it became lethal.

Her armor ignited, and a terrible pain flooded her mind.

The talons of the enormous thunderbird were moments away from snatching her.

But in the end, failed to reach her.

Burning, Jet fell into the sea of flames.

I wonder...

A moment later, she rolled across cold concrete in a cloud of smoke and crashed into a cracked wall, shattering it entirely. As pieces of concrete and dust fell on her from above, Jet coughed and let out a pained groan.

...am I the first Saint to escape from a Supreme?

No, come to think of it, Cassie had escaped too. Asterion seemed to have terrible luck with catching Saint.

Jet, on the other hand, had been quite lucky.

She had returned to the waking world.

Chapter 2827: Critical Mass

Chapter 2827: Critical Mass

Even after escaping the Dream Realm, Jet was under no illusion that she was safe now.

In fact, she was confident that since Asterion had come to capture her, he would have prepared an ambush in the government stronghold where she kept her tether, as well. He had already proven himself capable of being quite thorough during the attack on Cassie.

That was why she had secretly moved her tether to an undisclosed location weeks ago, with no one being the wiser. Not even the other members of Changing Stars cohort knew where she was tethered now, so there was little chance of the Dreamspawn tracing her current location quickly.

He would find her eventually, though, so Jet had little time to waste.

Taking a deep breath, she gritted her teeth and sat up.

Her armor had been burned to a crisp and was already collapsing into a rain of dancing sparks. Beneath it, the snow-white smoothness of her skin was interspersed with gruesome burns. A good portion of her body was scorched and blackened, creating a ghastly sight.

Jet exhaled a small cloud of smoke and smiled darkly.

At least she was alive.

Well... maybe not quite alive. But definitely in one piece.

[Close your eyes, Jet.]

Hearing Cassies voice in her mind, Jet lingered for a moment and then did as she had been told.

[Why?]

There was a brief silence.

[I cannot be sure that the Dreamspawn has no access to my mind. So, it would be best if you dont show me where you are. After this conversation is over, I will erase my mark and cut our connection.]

Jet let out a heavy sigh.

She briefly enjoyed the feeling of cold air caressing her burns, and then spoke quietly:

"I assume you already know what happened. The Night Garden... is lost. And that abomination seemed to have grown strong enough to easily sway Saints. Something changed."

Dar of the Maharana clan was the first Transcendent to fall under the Dreamspawns spell... or so they had thought. However, the plague had swallowed Red Hill too suddenly and too swiftly, leaving them suspicious. It was difficult to investigate what had happened because Mordret left no witnesses, but there were breadcrumbs to be found in the last messages of Saint Dar.

The people of Red Hill had suffered from insomnia caused by a persistent plague of nightmares. This clue led Nephis and her companions to Saint Thane, the Dream Merchant... who had been developing a new version of Dreamspace to serve as a way for distant Citadels of humanity to communicate with each other.

Jet, of course, was very familiar with the Dream Merchant, who had once been one of the two government Saints alongside Wake of Ruin.

It was unclear when Asterion had enthralled Saint Thane. What was clear, however, was that the unseen damage caused to the Human Domain by the infected dreams was grave. It had accelerated the spread of the plague, making countless people across the Dream Realm far more susceptible to it. Red Hill had been targeted especially severely.

Much worse, the Dream Merchant had remained a subject of the Longing Domain until the very end, proving that Asterion was capable of far more than simply making his thralls blindly loyal to his cause.

After that discovery, Nephis and her allies could not even tell how many Saints had already fallen under Asterions hex.

But, still...

Enthralling all six Saints aboard the Night Garden including someone as stalwart as Tyris or as exceptionally predisposed to loathing the Dreamspawn as Nightwalker was too difficult a feat. It had all happened too fast.

Cassie seemed to agree.

[It is most likely because of what happened at the Lake of Tears. The plague seems to have reached critical mass there. Now, its... unstoppable.]

Jet was sitting on the cold concrete with her eyes closed, as if meditating. Her body was like a morbidly beautiful painting, white and black hues accentuated by streaks of vibrant red. Her expression was somber.

She remained silent for a while, then said in an even tone:

"Since the Night Garden has fallen... Bastion and Ravenheart will follow soon."

Her voice sounded hoarse in the cold darkness.

Cassies answer was delayed by a few seconds.

[It seems that way. In fact...]

She paused for a moment, and then added calmly:

[I lost track of the Night Garden. So, an attack on the Ivory Tower seems imminent as well.]

A dark grimace contorted Jets face.

"So... what am I supposed to do now? Every countermeasure I can think of is bound to end up being an exercise in futility."

Cassie remained silent for a while before responding.

[Put your faith in Nephis and Sunny. Hide and survive until they return.]

Jet chuckled.

"I cannot really lie low, Cassie. If I do, my essence will run out, and Ill die. No matter where Ill go, there needs to be something for me to kill there."

Cassie had to know it, as well.

[Escape NQSC for now. It is not safe there anymore... Ill provide an escape route. Once you are not in immediate danger, you can think of a way to satiate your Flaw.]

Receiving the instructions on where to go, Jet smiled bitterly.

"How ironic. But I like it, actually... thats the last place they will look, considering the circumstances."

She fell silent for a moment, then asked:

"What about you?"

Cassies response sounded confident, but she could sense a hint of tension in it.

[If worst comes to worst... I have a few escape routes prepared, as well. Hopefully, though, I wont have to use them.]

Jet exhaled slowly.

For a few moments, there was nothing but silence in her mind.

"I guess youll be cutting the connection between us now, then?"

Cassie answered after a short pause:

[Yes. There is nothing left to say.]

Jet sighed again.

"...Take care of yourself, Cassie."

Just before she felt a familiar presence disappear from her mind, she suddenly asked:

"Wait... Nephis and the Lord of Shadows. Where are they, really?"

There was a moment of silence, and then Cassie chuckled.

[I dont know.]

Jet scoffed.

[I dont know, because I erased my own memories of having known where they went. So, even if the Dreamspawn captures me, he wont find out.]

She fell silent for a moment.

[Take care of yourself as well, Jet.]

With that, Cassie was gone.

Jet had never really known when their seer was sharing her senses, but now, she suddenly felt lonely in her own mind.

A moment later, her icy blue eyes gleamed in the darkness.

"Right. Lets escape NQSC, then..."

Chapter 2828: Escape from NQSC

Chapter 2828: Escape from NQSC

Now that most residents of the outskirts left for the Dream Realm, the vast human hives that had teemed with life and desperation stood mostly empty. There were still people living there, though even if some dormitory towers only had a few dozen inhabitants instead of tens of thousands.

A family that had once sheltered in a single residential cell now occupied an entire block. Even then, the rest of the floor was empty.

In the dim twilight of the early dawn, a gaunt man emerged into a corridor and leaned on the wall, contorted in a violent coughing fit. His wife was already busy boiling water to hydrate packs of synthpaste for the kids however, he had to put on his work uniform and depart for an early shift.

Wiping his lips, he stumbled toward the laundry room.

A few moments later, however, he froze and looked ahead in horror.

Out there in front of him, the claustrophobic expanse of the dormitory tower was drowning in cold mist, and for a brief moment, he saw a ghostly silhouette moving through it.

Flesh as pale as that of a corpse, harrowing burns that seeped with scarlet blood...

Screaming, the man staggered away.

"Gghost! Ghost!"

Turning around, he ran as if his life depended on it.

A few moments after the man fled, a pale arm extended from the mist toward the clothesline.

Its like I came full circle.

Jet had grown up in a dormitory hive very much like this one, surrounded by gaunt people with waxy skin who were prone to coughing fits. She had been sickly and neglected, as well, wearing clothes that were threadbare and did not fit her frail figure.

Some clothes were better than no clothes, though.

Putting on a pair of worn pants, a shabby shirt, and a ragged coat, she grimaced when the coarse fabric scraped against her burns and turned into mist. Soon, she was on the ground floor of the dormitory tower, hiding in the shadows of the back entrance awning and looking up.

Out there in the pale sky above NQSC, a storm of crows was painting mesmerizing patterns among clouds as it flowed in a vast murmuration.

Her expression darkened.

Old man...

Jet could tell a lot about what was going on in the city just from how it sounded. On this hazy morning, there were sounds of armored PTVs rolling on the asphalt, sirens howling in the distance, and the hum of sharp voices calling out to each other, muffled by the distance.

These particular noises were different from the usual clamor of the city, as well as from the panicked urgency of an opening Gate. As someone who had been the governments enforcer for many years, Jet knew the nature of this rough melody too well.

This was the sound of a large-scale manhunt.

Things like that happened rarely, since the government preferred to solve most issues quietly. However, she had led a few of such manhunts herself.

Today, Jet was quite sure that the person being hunted... was her.

Finding herself on the other side of law enforcement felt strange.

She traced the murmurations of the crows for a few moments, then looked away so that Wake of Ruin did not sense her gaze.

Is he enthralled, too?

Even if Jet did not want to believe it, she had an ominous feeling that the person in charge of hunting her down was none other than Old Cor. There were too many signs that pointed at him... and even if there werent, preparing for the worst had never failed her in the past. The world had nothing but the worst in store for the people born in the era of the Nightmare Spell, after all.

Getting to her destination unnoticed while Wake of Ruin was watching the city from high above would be difficult.

Muttering a quiet curse, Jet hid deeper in the shadows and collapsed into a torrent of mist.

She traveled into the depths of the city while hiding her presence as best she could. When it was possible, she moved underground. When the patrolling Awakened got too close, she avoided them. When a barrier stood in her way, she passed through it like a wraith.

Catching a ghost in the cauldron of human souls as vast as NQSC was not easy, even for the powerful machinery of the government and its oldest champion, Wake of Ruin. Especially if that ghost knew every gear of that complicated machine by heart.

That said... the city was different from how it had been the last time she visited.

It was in the throes of internal conflict. The streets were strangely desolate. Here and there, burning vehicles were scattered on the roads. Groups of soldiers were moving between them, wearing grim expressions. Many buildings were gaping with broken windows, pieces of furniture and debris spilling on the pavements.

In some places, the ground was smeared with blood.

The noise of the city was wrong and unhealthy, as if NQSC was being consumed by fever.

Its all going south.

The sun had already risen by the time Jet made it to where Cassie had sent her.

In front of her was the heavily fortified government compound in the heart of the city the very place where Jet had been anchored before secretly moving her tether to the desolate ruin in the outskirts.

She had gone to all the trouble to escape it, so naturally, the Dreamspawn and his servants would not expect that she would immediately return here. In that sense, her destination alone had helped her remain unnoticed.

The government compound was in disarray. The gates were open, and there were no guards posted outside. Smoke was billowing from the windows of several levels... which meant that the automatic defence systems had either malfunctioned or were disabled, failing to execute a lockdown protocol.

Most tellingly of all, there were muffled sounds of gunshots and heavy impacts resounding from inside.

Jet assumed her human form and walked across the broken asphalt barefoot, her ragged coat fluttering in the wind.

Her expression was unamused.

"I leave for a bit, and the whole place is a mess..."

Stepping over the unconscious body of an Awakened soldier, she entered the compound.

Chapter 2829: Abandon Ship

Chapter 2829: Abandon Ship

The familiar lobby of the government compound was uncharacteristically empty... except for the corpses.

The walls were cracked and riddled with holes. The furniture was destroyed. The floor and the ceiling were splattered with blood.

Jet regarded the scene of devastation with a distant expression. It seemed like there had been a firefight here recently... mundane soldiers had clashed with each other at first, and were then wiped out by the Awakened.

The battle had moved on deeper into the building since then.

Judging by the sounds and the mild tremors running through the floor, only sporadic skirmishes were still happening on the upper floors of the compound, while most of the violence was happening underground.

In all the years since its establishment, the government complex in NQSC had never been breached yet now, it seemed to have fallen.

However, the compound had not been attacked from outside. The scene of the lobby told Jet that much... it had been compromised from within.

The thralls of Asterion who had been hidden among the government personnel must have finally turned on those of their comrades who still remained loyal to the Human Domain. The Dreamspawn was tired of waiting and had the means to take control, since most of humanity had already fallen to his plague... so, he gave his servants a command to finish the job forcefully.

Frowning in displeasure, Jet made her way into the depths of the compound. She grimaced as she walked, the pain of her burns radiating across her body like heat.

Her wounds were painful, but not life-threatening. Even if they were, Jet was not quite alive, so they would not have threatened her existence. Still, she wished that Nephis would heal them, already... sadly, Nephis could not heal every minor scrape. If she did, she would have been overcome by an endless, relentless agony.

So, Jet had to endure the pain until her Transcendent body naturally repaired itself in a few days. Cursing quietly, she made her way forward.

The emergency systems of the complex had been shut down, so the elevators werent working. The stairwells had become strategic avenues for control over the building most of them were in the hands of the turncoats, who were besieging the few underground levels where the remaining loyalists had barricaded themselves.

Jet wanted to help, but knew that revealing herself would only bring death and destruction upon them. So, she simply passed through the closed doors of an elevator and drifted down its dark shaft as a wraith.

The deeper she went, the louder the sounds of the battle were.

Eventually, she exited the shaft on one of the deepest levels of the government complex.

The turncoats seemed to have retreated from here temporarily, leaving behind dozens of corpses. Each of the dead men had been killed by one precise shot that struck the weak points of their armor with eerie precision.

The floor was slick with blood.

Jet coalesced into a human and studied the corpses with a dispassionate expression. Then, sensing an intense gaze, she looked into the depths of the long corridor.

"Do you think your bullets can harm me?"

A woman of unassuming appearance revealed herself from the shadows, lowering a combat rifle. She was wearing a dark suit of enchanted combat armor, and her cold gaze was both piercing and calm.

The woman regarded Jet for a moment, then bowed slightly.

"Saint Jet. I am Awakened Kim. Webe been told to expect you."

Jet headed toward Awakened Kim with measured steps.

"I take it the evacuation is not going well?"

The woman shook her head.

"Everything is on schedule. You are the last one to arrive, though, so we must hurry. Follow me, please."

Together, they left the bloodied corridor behind and proceeded to the doors of a massive cargo elevator. The doors had been locked, but the seal was broken as were the doors themselves. Something immensely powerful seemed to have torn them apart.

A pair of winches had been installed at the mouth of the vertical shaft, steel cables falling into the darkness.

Awakened, Kim proficiently strapped herself to a descender, slung the rifle to her back, and began to rappel down without saying anything. Jet simply turned into a wraith and followed her by levitating in the air.

The shaft was quite long. As they descended into the depths of the earth, Jet asked in an ethereal, echoing voice:

"Are members of the Shadow Clan not susceptible to the plague?"

Awakened Kim glanced at her briefly.

"We are, even if our resistance to it is quite high. After all, each of us knows our Sovereign personally unlike the subjects of the Longing Domain, for most of whom Lady Nephis is merely an abstract symbol. Still, we did lose a few agents to the Hunger Domain, already. Its just that identifying them is far easier for us."

She stopped for a moment to catch her breath and nodded to her forearm, where a small sliver of a serpent tattoo was visible between the edge of her vambrace and the lip of her black glove.

"The Mark of Shadows rejects them. Its hard to miss."

Jet smiled.

A method like that did not guarantee absolute safety, but the Shadow Clan was indeed more immune to the plague than anyone else in the world. Better yet, their lands were separated from the rest of the Human Domain by the Hollow Mountains. There were currently only three ways to reach the Forgotten Shore.

One was to cross the Hollow Mountains even if Asterion was capable of doing that, it would take him a considerable amount of time. The second was to be carried across the realm boundary by Dark Dancer Revel, who had been marked by the Lord of Shadows.

And the third way...

Just then, they reached the bottom of the immensely long elevator shaft.

In front of them was a vast underground chamber, so tall that its ceiling could barely be seen far above.

And in the center of that chamber, a black rift towered like a wound in the fabric of the world.

The Dream Gate of the Lord of Shadows.

One of the seven Gates he could open, and the only one he had left behind for his servants to use.

Detaching herself from the descender harness, Awakened Kim looked at her watch.

"We still have thirteen minutes left. Everyone, hurry! We depart in ten!"

There were other people in the chamber, clad in suits of armor similar to hers. They were currently busy loading supply crates and various equipment on primitive alloy wagons, ready to push them into the Gate.

There was someone else in the chamber, as well someone Jet had not expected to see.

Or rather... something else?

A dreadful black steed was standing beside the Dream Gate, watching the entrance to the shaft with his frightening crimson eyes.

There was something different about him today, though. As Jet studied the Terror, she noticed a familiar iron locket hanging on a black leather cord around his neck.

She raised an eyebrow.

"Whats that horse doing here?"

Awakened Kim looked at the black stallion respectfully.

"Lord Nightmare just showed up."

Jet hesitated for a few moments, then decided to move on and asked a different question instead:

"And what will happen in thirteen minutes?"

Kim looked at her watch again.

"Twelve minutes now."

She lingered for a moment and then said in a reserved tone:

"We are retreating from the waking world, and no one should be able to follow us. So, in twelve minutes, the Dream Gate will shut down. Today is the deadline set for us by our boss."

Which meant that they would be completely cut from the rest of humanity after passing through the Gate the only member of the Shadow Clan who could travel between the worlds freely was Revel herself.

Jet sighed.

"Good thing I arrived on time, then."

The minutes seemed to stretch endlessly until, finally, it was time to leave.

Just then, Jet heard an ominous sound coming from the shaft.

It was the sound of countless wings beating as a swarm of crows flew down.

"Move, now!"

The wagons were pushed into the Gate. The members of the Shadow Clan dove into its darkness, as well Awakened Kim was the last one to pass the threshold.

Jet did not want to have to kill her old mentor, so he rushed forward.

"What are you waiting for? Need a special invitation?"

The dreadful steed of the Lord of Shadows spared her a chilling look, then glanced at the shaft and snorted. Then, he followed Jet into the dark expanse of the Dream Gate.

No sooner did they emerge on the other side than the black rift of the Gate rippled... and disappeared without a trace.

Jet let out a long sigh and leaned on the side of the monstrous horse, catching her breath.

She could relax a little, since she had finally escaped the clutches of the Dreamspawn.

Around her, the Dark City of the Forgotten Shore basked in impenetrable darkness.

Chapter 2830: Over the Hills and Far Away

Chapter 2830: Over the Hills and Far Away

Not long before that, Effie had a nice breakfast with her family. Little Ling was boasting about his studies, while her husband was listening to him quietly and chuckling from time to time.

"Oh? Did you hear that, dear? Our son is interested in history now. Didnt you mention that you were fond of history too, when you were little?"

Ling stared at her thoughtfully.

"Huh? Mom was little once?"

Effie scoffed.

"Yeah, well. I couldnt really go anywhere when I was a kid, so I read everything I could get my hands on. I liked history too."

Her husband took her hand.

"You hear that, rascal? Not only was your mom little once, but she was also a bookworm..."

Soon enough, the breakfast was over, and its warm atmosphere dissipated. Effie saw her husband off to the gates of their estate and kissed him goodbye. He had business to attend to in the city today, while she was supposed to depart for the Castle after handing Little Ling off to his tutor.

Instead of hurrying back inside, however, Effie remained motionless for a while, looking at the street.

Then, she sighed and turned away.

Entering their home, she called Ling and sat him down in front of her.

"Hey there, dumpling. Were you excited for your lessons today?"

He hesitated for a few moments, then asked instead of answering:

"Whats wrong, mom?"

Her smile faltered for a moment.

"Wrong? Nothing is wrong. Its just that I want you to do something for me."

Little Ling nodded.

"Of course! What is it?"

Effie pulled the Black Beast Locket, which was hanging around her neck, out.

"You see... Uncle Sunny is away right now. So, Auntie Aiko is all alone in a huge castle. I was thinking that maybe youll go keep her company for a bit... what do you think about that?"

Little Lings eyes ignited with enthusiasm.

"Really? Can I really go? Really?!"

Effie nodded with a smile, then patted his head.

"Sure. Oh, and that castle? Its a bit scary, but actually... the castle is alive. It can even walk around."

The boys eyes widened.

"Wait. Uncle Sunny had such a cool castle this whole time, and he never even invited me once?"

Effie chuckled.

"Well, you can go take a look now."

Little Ling raised his fists into the air.

"Yes! I cant wait to tell dad!"

A subtle shadow ran across Effies face.

"You cant tell dad yet. Once Uncle Sunny is back, Ill come pick you up. You can report your findings to us then like an explorer. Okay?"

Little Ling suddenly seemed unsure.

"Uh... what, we are leaving right now? What about dad? What about my lessons?"

Instead of answering, Effie placed her hand on his shoulder. The locket hanging around her neck shimmered and collapsed into a rain of sparks, which then flowed like a torrent into Little Lings chest.

"Its a bit dark where the castle is, so if you want to go somewhere sunny, just hop inside the Beast Farm. Okay? Actually, why dont you go there right now? Take a walk and then nap a little. By the time you come out, youll already be with Auntie Aiko."

Little Ling seemed frozen in place.

"Mom! You gave me a Memory! Its your locket, mom!"

Effie patted him on the head.

"Take good care of it for me, alright?"

Some time later, Ling was safely hidden inside the Black Beast Locket. Picking it up from the floor, Effie sighed and then closed her eyes.

The realm boundary parted in front of her, and she appeared in the waking world.

Her absence would be noticed soon... in fact, she was willing to bet that the Dreamspawn was watching her every move. So, she could not be seen delivering the Black Beast Locket to its destination.

Instead, she looked at her shadow and said quietly:

"Come out."

A moment later, two crimson flames ignited in the darkness, and an enormous black steed rose from it, looking at her with chilling intensity.

Walking up to the tenebrous stallion, Effie untied the cord of the Black Beast Locket and then tied it carefully around his neck.

"Bring him to the Forgotten Shore... to Aiko. Make sure that no one sees you."

The black steed snorted in protest.

"I know that you were ordered to protect Bastion, Little Ling, and me. But I am telling you to do this instead. Sunny would have agreed if he were here, so go."

The stallion stared at her for a few moments, then briefly pressed his nose against her shoulder and dissolved into the shadows.

Left alone, Effie sighed heavily and then reached for her tether.

Nightmare was protecting Little Ling... so, it was up to her to protect Bastion and herself.

I just hope... that I am wrong.

But soon enough, she learned that she hadnt been.

***

"Auntie Jet! Were leaving!"

Jet looked up, at the battlements of the Dark Castle. There, a boy was waving at her with a hint of sadness on his face. Only a hint, though mostly, he seemed thrilled.

The little rascal had been heartbroken when he learned that she would not be coming with them, but now, he looked quite happy.

She waved back, wondering when she would see him again.

If she would see him ever again.

It had already been a few days since she arrived on the Forgotten Shore, and now, it was time to say farewell. Little Ling was going on an exciting adventure...

Jet, meanwhile, was going to try and not succumb to her Flaw.

There was a rustle of wings, and Revel landed beside her, wearing her usual cold expression. Jet glanced at the former princess of Song, noting the Black Beast Locket hanging around her neck.

"Look at you, Lightslayer. Taking toys from children."

Revel looked down at her and smiled darkly.

"Dont worry, Reaper. Ill be giving it right back."

Jet lingered for a few moments and then asked:

"So, how did it go?"

Revel shrugged nonchalantly and raised her arm, where the coils of a serpent tattoo were clearly visible.

"I still have my wits about me, if thats what youre asking. The prisoners have been delivered to the authorities, as well."

She sighed.

"My career as a prison warden did not last long. Thank the dead gods."

Now that the Forgotten Shore had become a shelter for the members of the Shadow Clan, keeping thousands of Asterions thralls here did not seem like a good idea. The very reason why they had been captured trying to slow down the spreading plague was now meaningless, as well.

So, Revel had carried them to the waking world in the Black Beast Locket and released them. Their brief, but memorable imprisonment was over, just as inexplicably as it had started.

Still, the thralls had seen the walls of the Dark City, which meant that Asterion knew that the forces of the Shadow Clan were present here. In order to be safe, Revel had decided to move the Dark Castle somewhere else.

Jet raised an eyebrow.

"So, where are you going?"

Reveil shrugged.

"The Forgotten Shore is vast. I think the Mimic will just have to be a wandering castle for a while. What about you, Reaper? Where are you going?"

She paused for a moment and then asked:

"Are you sure you dont want to stay?"

Jet smiled faintly.

"It has nothing to do with what I want. Pretty soon, Ill need to kill something... and theres nothing to kill on the Forgotten Shore."

She looked west.

"So, Ive been thinking of going west, into the frozen wastelands. Who knows? I might even come back alive."

Jet looked at Revel and grinned.

"Well, maybe not quite... ah, wait. You dont know."

There was no one here she could joke about being dead with.

Suddenly missing the Lord of Shadows, Jet patted Revel on the side and pointed to the Dark Castle.

"Godspeed, Lightslayer. Go, the little knave cant wait to ride a living castle."

Revel studied her for a moment before nodding.

"I have a feeling we wont see each other for a while. Dont go entirely feral out there, Reaper... take care."

With that, she soared into the air and flew toward the walls of the Dark Castle.

Soon enough, enormous legs extended from beneath the menacing fortress, and it began climbing down the slope of the steep hill. There was no giant moth sitting atop its main tower, but Jet still couldnt help but remember the dizzying assault on the Eternal City.

How the hell is that thing going to climb over the wall?

She was left alone in the darkness.

Shaking her head, Jet turned away and headed in the opposite direction.

Soul essence kept trickling from her broken core, and with it, life was slowly leaving her body.

Jet walked through the Dark City, which was quiet and empty. She ascended the wall and jumped down from it, turning into a torrent of mist just before landing.

A few moments later, she assumed her human form again and regarded the boundless darkness ahead of her wistfully.

Somewhere far away, the frozen wastelands were waiting to embrace her in their frigid embrace. Nobody knew where they led, and how far the Hollow Mountains extended into them. If she were lucky, she would return from the endless blizzard stronger and more powerful.

If not... she would not return at all.

Letting out a sigh, Jet took the first step.

A torrent of ethereal sparks appeared above her shoulder, slowly forming into a black crow.

The crow flapped its wings and opened its beak, cawing loudly:

"Dark! Dark!"

Jet nodded.

"Yeah, you stupid bird. Hey, why dont you wish me some luck?"

Crow Crow remained silent for a few moments, and then opened its wings wide.

"...Luck! Luck!"

Chapter 2831: Memory Key

Chapter 2831: Memory Key

Cassie surfaced from the torrent of torturous memories.

Her consciousness reeled from the bleak terror of the scenes and sensations captured in them. Even though she did not seem to have a mouth, her tongue was burning with a bitter taste... the taste of defeat, betrayal, and hopelessness.

The Tower of Hope had fallen into the enemys hands, and the guiding star of mankind was absent. What kind of hope could there be?

Ah...

She let out an anguished groan.

At least... at least Jet escaped...

She had sent her to the Dream Gate before erasing the mark.

Cassie could see it all now the grand, harrowing visage of the plague.

The Dreamspawn had been sealed on the Moon by the Sovereigns. They had slaughtered those who knew his name and erased all traces of him from the world, going so far as to hide themselves in the shadows to prevent people from remembering Asterion.

No... not all traces. Even with their vast power and uncontested authority, erasing the records of his existence completely would have been impossible. The network could be manipulated easily, but anything committed to paper would have to be found first. Even then, rewriting history too aggressively would have only served to shine a spotlight on the fact that something was being covered up.

And, therefore, make people curious to learn what it was.

So, they made information about Asterion as sparse as possible and continuously culled those who fell under his influence. That was how they managed to keep him sealed.

...Of course, Asterion himself had not been in a hurry to return. He waited patiently, observing humanity from above as it slowly grew stronger until it was powerful enough to satiate his hunger.

The Sovereigns were gone by then, and the young Supremes who had usurped their thrones were ignorant both of the extent of the threat Asterion represented and of how to keep him at bay... precisely because all knowledge about him had been erased by their predecessors.

So, he exerted his influence from the Moon, infecting a few people with a subconscious impulse to spread his name. That was how the plague started, and how his Domain and therefore his power began to grow.

Eventually, Asterion returned from the Moon. He let his existence be known and endeavored to undermine the foundations of the Human Domain. The new Supremes could not stop him because he was holding all of humanity hostage...

And by holding it hostage, he ensured that the plague continued to spread until all of humanity fell under his spell.

Mundane people, Awakened, Ascended, and Saints everyone was enthralled by the Dreamspawn. The Great Citadels of humanity fell into his hands. Effie and Kai were captured, while Jet was forced to escape beyond the boundary of the Human Domain.

The only obstacle remaining in Asterions path... was Mordret. The mad Supreme who aimed to consume the Hunger Domain before the Hunger Domain could consume everything.

And Cassie herself, who escaped the Hunger Domain to stand by Mordrets side.

So where...

Where were Nephis and Sunny? Why had they left? What could have forced them to abandon their people, their kingdom, and even their friends?

Cassie pulled back the tentacles of her Will and regarded the dark ocean of memories with intense focus.

Now, her gaze seemed to penetrate the fragmented memories, instantly sensing their nature. In front of her were the memories of her own short life, shared with the memories of experiencing the lives of others. There were memories she had glimpsed in the minds of those who looked into her eyes, as well as memories of the future she had destroyed.

There were also memories of the past a vast, harrowing expanse of them that belonged to all kinds of people and creatures, spanning from the dawn of time to the present day. From the Age of Gods to the Age of the Nightmare Spell, these memories told countless tales... the tales of those who had been forgotten.

Cassie did not know how she had come to possess them.

She did not want to know at the moment, either.

All she wanted was to find a single shard, a single memory one that could explain to her why Changing Star and the Lord of Shadows were missing. Everything else would make sense if she found that one memory, which was like a key to unlock the meaning of everything that had happened and was happening to her still.

And there...

I see...

She found it.

A small, seemingly insignificant shard was glistening dimly among the myriad of them.

This is the key.

Locking her gaze onto the tiny shard, Cassie shot the tentacles of her Will toward it like a vast tide.

Grasping it, she saw...

It happened soon after Asterion visited the Immortal Flame manor, and long before the plague had truly taken hold of humanity. Cassie was still in NQSC, even if she could not stay long one of Sunnys incarnations was hiding in her shadow, protecting her, so they had to leave soon.

Before that, however, Cassie wanted to visit the government archives, where the clues gathered in the ruins of the Clan Valor compound were being kept. There was little chance that she would find any hints about how to deal with Asterion there, but she still wanted to check.

Sadly, her search proved to be fruitless. In the end, she left the archives having learned nothing, a heavy feeling on her heart.

She felt like they were losing, and there was no hint of a solution in sight.

Disheartened, Cassie walked through the corridors of the government complex... until she stumbled on a familiar face.

An Awakened man was waiting for an appointment in a corridor. Cassie could not see his face, but recognized his scent. Hearing his breathing and heartbeat change, as well as the quiet rustle of his clothes as he changed posture, she determined that he was surprised and elated to see her.

"Lady Cassia, maam!"

She paused and turned to face him, seeing her own pale face and the blue blindfold covering her eyes through his own.

She lingered for a moment.

"Awakened Yutra. What a coincidence... it is nice to see you."

Indeed, it was Yutra her former subordinate and the first of Asterions thralls she had cured of the plague.

He seemed to have smiled.

"Oh, yes. You too!"

Yutra remained silent for a bit, then said awkwardly:

"It is really nice to see you, maam. After the facility closed... well, life has been a bit chaotic for me. Because of the missing memories, you know? But, still. I hope you know that I all of us, actually are proud to have been able to assist you. With, uh... whatever it was we were really doing there."

Cassie couldnt help but smile.

"Thank you. I am proud to have received your assistance, as well."

Embarrassed by her words, Yutra chucked.

He remained silent for a short while, and then said suddenly:

"Actually... you probably dont remember... but weve met once before a long time ago, when you were only a Master. The famous Lady Cassia! For me, it was very memorable. So that was why, while working at the facility... well, I felt like fate brought me there. Uh. What I mean to say is..."

Cassie tilted her head, listening to him silently.

...Weve met before?

She had delved into Yutras memories many times, but never into his memories before the fall of the Sovereigns. There was simply no reason to, since he had only learned the name of Asterion later.
